hints: Evaluate at $x = 2$ to find gradient $-\frac{2}{9}$, giving normal gradient $\frac{9}{2}$.
Form normal equation $y - 1 = \frac{9}{2}(x - 2)$ and set $y = 0$ to show $x = \frac{16}{9}$.
walkthrough:
Differentiate $y = 3(1 + 4x)^{-1/2}$ with respect to $x$ using the chain rule:
$$\frac{dy}{dx} = 3\left(-\frac{1}{2}\right)(1 + 4x)^{-3/2} \times (4) = -6(1 + 4x)^{-3/2} = -\frac{6}{(1 + 4x)^{3/2}}$$

Determine the gradient of the normal line perpendicular to the curve:
$$m_{\text{normal}} = -\frac{1}{-2/9} = \frac{9}{2}$$

Write the equation of the normal line through $P(2, 1)$ and set $y = 0$ to find the $x$-intercept $Q$:
$$y - 1 = \frac{9}{2}(x - 2)$$
$$0 - 1 = \frac{9}{2}(x - 2) \implies x - 2 = -\frac{2}{9} \implies x = 2 - \frac{2}{9} = \frac{16}{9}$$

hints: Calculate triangle area under normal from $Q(16/9, 0)$ to $x = 2$: $\frac{1}{2}\left(2 - \frac{16}{9}\right)(1) = \frac{1}{9}$.
walkthrough:
Set up and evaluate the definite integral for the total area under the curve from $x = 0$ to $x = 2$:
$$\text{Area}_{\text{curve}} = \int_0^2 3(1 + 4x)^{-1/2}\,dx = \left[ 3 \times \frac{(1 + 4x)^{1/2}}{\frac{1}{2} \times 4} \right]_0^2 = \left[ \frac{3}{2}\sqrt{1 + 4x} \right]_0^2$$
$$\text{Area}_{\text{curve}} = \frac{3}{2}\sqrt{1 + 4(2)} - \frac{3}{2}\sqrt{1 + 0} = \frac{3}{2}(3) - \frac{3}{2}(1) = \frac{9}{2} - \frac{3}{2} = 3$$

Calculate the area of the right-angled triangle bounded by the normal line, the $x$-axis, and the vertical line $x = 2$:
$$\text{Base} = 2 - \frac{16}{9} = \frac{2}{9}, \quad \text{Height} = 1$$
$$\text{Area}_{\text{triangle}} = \frac{1}{2} \times \text{base} \times \text{height} = \frac{1}{2} \times \frac{2}{9} \times 1 = \frac{1}{9}$$

Subtract the triangle area from the area under the curve:
$$\text{Shaded Area} = \text{Area}_{\text{curve}} - \text{Area}_{\text{triangle}} = 3 - \frac{1}{9} = \frac{26}{9} = 2\frac{8}{9} \quad (\approx 2.89)$$
